questions.q: In ethers.js v6, what type does provider.getBalance() return?
options: A native bigint
The custom BigNumber class from ethers v5
A regular JavaScript number
A string
questions.explain: ethers v6 dropped the custom BigNumber class used in v5 and returns native bigint everywhere a chain value could overflow number, including getBalance.

questions.q: How does viem create a read-only client, in contrast to ethers' class-based Provider?
options: With `new PublicClient(...)`, the same way ethers uses `new JsonRpcProvider(...)`
With a factory function, createPublicClient({...}), returning a typed PublicClient object — no `new`
viem has no concept of a read-only client
By importing a global `client` singleton that can't be configured
questions.explain: viem is functional, not class-based — createPublicClient is a factory function that returns a typed client object, unlike ethers' `new JsonRpcProvider(...)` pattern.

questions.q: What is the difference between ethers' TransactionResponse and TransactionReceipt types?
options: They are the same type with two different names
TransactionReceipt is only used for failed transactions
TransactionResponse represents a broadcast transaction; TransactionReceipt represents one that has been mined, with guaranteed fields like blockNumber and status
TransactionResponse is returned only by viem, never ethers
questions.explain: A transaction that's been sent but not yet mined is a TransactionResponse; once mined, tx.wait() resolves to a TransactionReceipt, which carries fields like blockNumber and status that only exist after mining.

questions.q: In viem, what builds a WalletClient capable of sending a transaction?
options: Calling .connect() on a PublicClient
viem does not support sending transactions, only reading
Passing a raw hex string directly as the transport
An `account` — either a local private-key account (privateKeyToAccount) or an injected wallet — passed into createWalletClient
questions.explain: createWalletClient takes an `account` (from privateKeyToAccount for a local key, or an address from an injected provider) plus a chain and transport, producing a client that can sign and send.

questions.q: What is the core API design difference between ethers v6 and viem, given that both use bigint for on-chain amounts?
options: ethers only works in the browser; viem only works in Node.js
ethers uses class instances with method-call syntax (contract.balanceOf()); viem uses factory-built client objects with explicit function calls (readContract({...}))
viem doesn't support TypeScript at all
ethers requires bigint; viem still uses BigNumber
questions.explain: Both libraries settled on bigint for chain values — the real difference is shape: ethers' Provider/Signer/Contract are classes built with `new` and called as methods, while viem's PublicClient/WalletClient are plain objects from factory functions, with contract calls passed as explicit arguments.
